This petition is filed by the accused assailing the order passed on discharge application filed under Section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking discharge NC: 2025:KHC-K:7392 HC-KAR for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 376, 504, 506 and 417 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. Facts leading to the case are as under:
The prosecution case, in brief, is that the victim is a widow who lost her husband in a road traffic accident, and thereafter secured compassionate appointment in the North-West Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation, where she was initially posted at Shahapur Depot.

sentences.text: Based on these allegations, a complaint was lodged, culminating in registration of the crime and submission of a charge sheet after investigation.

Upon receipt of summons, the petitioner appeared before the Sessions Court and filed an application under Section 239 of Cr.P.C. seeking discharge.
The specific contention urged was that the relationship between the complainant and the petitioner was consensual, and that the allegations of sexual assault were fabricated.

In support of this plea, reliance was placed upon the further statement of the complainant as well as the statements of her brother and three prosecution witnesses, who had deposed before the Investigating Officer that the complainant and the accused were in a consensual relationship and that the petitioner had expressed his intention to marry her.
4. The Public Prosecutor contested the application.
The learned Sessions Judge, upon consideration of the charge-sheet material, was of the view that sufficient grounds existed to proceed against the petitioner.

According to the Court, the complaint specifically alleged that the petitioner had raped the victim NC: 2025:KHC-K:7392 HC-KAR at knife-point against her will, and this allegation was supported, in the Court's view, by the medical records.

The learned Judge observed that the mere noting in the medical report that there were no signs of recent sexual intercourse would not, at the stage of consideration under Section 239 Cr.P.C., warrant discharge.
Consequently, the application was rejected.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner, reiterating the grounds urged before the Sessions Court,
placed emphasis on the further statement of the complainant wherein she is said to have retracted from her earlier allegation that the accused used to hold a knife and force her into sexual relations.

6. He further relied upon the statement of the complainant's brother, cited as C.W.4, who admitted having knowledge that the complainant and the accused were in a relationship and that the accused intended to marry her.
Similar statements, it is contended, were given NC: 2025:KHC-K:7392 HC-KAR by C.W.5--the wife of C.W.4and C.W.6.
Learned counsel also invited attention to the statement made by the complainant before the doctor acknowledging that she was in a love affair with the petitioner.

7. In light of these materials, learned counsel submitted that the case at its highest discloses a consensual relationship and that allegations of a false promise to marry, even if accepted, do not by themselves constitute an offence of rape unless the promise was made with dishonest intention from the inception.
Placing reliance on judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, he argued that the allegations do not satisfy the ingredients necessary to constitute an offence under Section 376 IPC.

Although the complaint contains grave allegations to the effect that on 06.02.2023 at about 7:00 p.m. the accused forcibly entered the complainant's residence, threatened her with a knife, and raped her, this version stands materially diluted and contradicted by her subsequent statement, wherein she retracts the allegations relating to coercion at knife-point.

sentences.text: Thus, upon a holistic appreciation of the chargesheet materials, this Court is of the considered view that the ingredients constituting the offence under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code are not disclosed.

The legal position laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgments cited by the learned counsel for the petitioner is squarely attracted to the facts of the present case, lending further support to the petitioner's plea for discharge.

18. The main reasoning adopted by the learned Sessions Judge that the complainant was subjected to - 18 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7392 HC-KAR rape at knife-point against her will clearly suffers from manifest perversity.
This finding is wholly inconsistent with the complainant's further statement and stands directly contradicted by her own admission before the doctor (C.W.16).
The learned Sessions Judge failed to take into account these material contradictions and the implications arising therefrom.

In circumstances where the chargesheet records themselves prima facie indicate the absence of the essential ingredients of the alleged offences, particularly the offence of rape, the continuation of criminal proceedings would amount to a miscarriage of justice.
This Court is therefore of the view that the impugned order reflects non-application of mind and is legally unsustainable, warranting interference in exercise of revisional jurisdiction.
19. For the foregoing reasons, and with a view to prevent abuse of the process of law, this Court finds it just - 19 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7392 HC-KAR and appropriate to interdict further proceedings.

Accordingly, the following order is passed:

(ii) The impugned order dated 04.07.2025 passed on the application under Section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Vijayapur in S.C.No.127/2024 is set aside.

In support of this plea, reliance was placed upon the further statement of the complainant as well as the statements of her brother and three prosecution witnesses, who had deposed before the Investigating Officer that the complainant and the accused were in a consensual relationship and that the petitioner had expressed his intention to marry her.
4. The Public Prosecutor contested the application.
The learned Sessions Judge, upon consideration of the charge-sheet material, was of the view that sufficient grounds existed to proceed against the petitioner.
Consequently, the application was rejected.

"Whether the learned Sessions Judge erred in rejecting the application for discharge by holding that there is sufficient material to proceed against the accused, despite the further statement of the complainant and the statements of C.Ws.4, 5 and 6 suggesting a consensual relationship between the parties?"

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Although the complaint contains grave allegations to the effect that on 06.02.2023 at about 7:00 p.m. the accused forcibly entered the complainant's residence, threatened her with a knife, and raped her, this version stands materially diluted and contradicted by her subsequent statement, wherein she retracts the allegations relating to coercion at knife-point.
Thus, upon a holistic appreciation of the chargesheet materials, this Court is of the considered view that the ingredients constituting the offence under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code are not disclosed.
This finding is wholly inconsistent with the complainant's further statement and stands directly contradicted by her own admission before the doctor (C.W.16).
The learned Sessions Judge failed to take into account these material contradictions and the implications arising therefrom.
In circumstances where the chargesheet records themselves prima facie indicate the absence of the essential ingredients of the alleged offences, particularly the offence of rape, the continuation of criminal proceedings would amount to a miscarriage of justice.
This Court is therefore of the view that the impugned order reflects non-application of mind and is legally unsustainable, warranting interference in exercise of revisional jurisdiction.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER
(i) The Criminal Revision Petition is hereby allowed.
(ii) The impugned order dated 04.07.2025 passed on the application under Section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Vijayapur in S.C.No.127/2024 is set aside.
(iii) The petitioner/accused is discharged from the entire criminal proceedings in S.C.No.127/2024 pending before the IV Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Vijayapur, arising out of Crime No.48/2023 registered by the Vijayapur Women Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 376, 504, 506 and 417 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
Consequently, all further proceedings in the said case stand quashed.
